newsitem.title: YEMEN: Yemen says German hostages to go free soon.
newsitem.headline: Yemen says German hostages to go free soon.

text.p: Yemen's interior minister said on Monday said seven German tourists abducted by local tribesmen would soon be released, Sanaa radio reported.
It said Hussein Mohammad Arab, in a meeting with the German ambassador, said the hostages "will be released very soon."
"Arab told the ambassador that the hostages were in good health and the (Yemeni) leadership is keen on their safety," said the radio.
The seven men aged between 30 and 45 were kidnapped on Monday while riding motorcycles through the Wadi al-Dabaat area between Mahra and Hadramaut provinces.
A senior security official said earlier on Monday negotiations with the abductors were making progress and the tribesmen were seeking a government amnesty before freeing the hostages.

Official sources said the kidnappers, all local tribesmen, wanted to put pressure on the government to bring to justice an alleged Yemeni swindler who sold them smuggled cars brought in from Saudi Arabia and other Gulf states.
The sources said the abductors had telephoned local authorities to demand 12 million marks ($7 million) ransom for releasing the tourists.
But police in Hadramaut, 770 km (480 miles) east of Sanaa, denied the kidnappers were demanding a ransom.
Yemeni tribes with grievances against the government or foreign oil firms have kidnapped scores of tourists, diplomats or other foreigners in recent years to use as bargaining chips.
An American diplomat and a Saudi ambassador have been among the kidnap victims. There have been no reported casualties from the abductions and all the hostages have been released unharmed.
Some were rescued by security forces, others were set free.
